summary: Iteration 19 — Full-stack pass on Phase 3 (AI Relationship/Risk on 360° contact profile + unified Business Calendar) and Phase 4 (AI Meeting Notes + Operating Score). Backend: 12/12 pytest green in 13s (rescore incl. AI call, contact-birthday roundtrip, calendar shape + perm-gating, meeting text pipeline end-to-end producing 3 tasks, operating-score for owner/sales/finance). Frontend: owner login → contact profile /contacts/:id shows relationship-card, Re-score button populates {relationship_score, risk_score, reason, signals} live (verified Relationship=10, Risk=50 with signals chips rendered); /calendar loads 18 day sections / 156 events, all 5 filter chips (task filter isolates 147/147 events with 0 leaks, payment_due filter for sales shows '(0)'), 90 Overdue badges visible; /meetings paste-toggle reveals textarea, submit creates card that transitions from processing→done and dialog opens with AI-generated title/summary/key points/decisions/action items; /operating-score shows overall=13, all 4 category bars + 4 quick stats + 25 employee rows; sales session verified — 0 payment_due events in calendar and no outstanding money leaked. Meeting record button present (mic recording not automatable).
action_items: Optional: On /operating-score the Finance category shows 0 for owner in the demo tenant while Sales sees ~70 because the endpoint defaults collected=0.7 when can_finance is False (server.py:1074) — this actually causes non-finance roles to see a DIFFERENT finance score (a higher one). That's not a money leak, but the number is misleading for non-finance users. Consider returning `finance: null` (like `outstanding: null`) for non-finance users and rendering '—' on the frontend, so the number isn't quietly fabricated.
Optional: Frontend Calendar.js sets queryKey ['calendar'] with fixed `?days=45` — if you later want a range picker, add days to the key.

Optional: Meetings.js:99 sends explicit `Content-Type: multipart/form-data` header (without boundary). Most axios builds override this correctly when body is FormData, but it's safer to omit the Content-Type and let the browser set it with the boundary automatically.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1046-1111 operating_score — for non-finance users the `finance` category is silently computed from defaults (collected=0.7, overdue_inv=0 → score 70), not hidden. This is inconsistent with the correct `outstanding: None` hiding in stats. Consider either (a) returning finance: null for non-finance users, or (b) computing category from a non-financial signal. As-is, sales/production/etc. see a 'Finance' category score they can't actually influence and that isn't the real number.
server.py:951-991 process_meeting — no per-tenant rate limit or transcript size cap. A pasted 1MB transcript would be sent to the LLM verbatim. Consider clipping to ~40k chars before sending.

server.py:2275-2345 business_calendar — 'complaint' events use created_at (not a due-date), so they always land in the past section. That's OK given the -14d..+days window includes recent past, but they will never show in the 'upcoming' area. If desired, surface open complaints as 'today' items instead.

server.py:2327-2334 birthday computation — uses `now.year` only; if a birthday's MM-DD falls in the last 14 days (already passed this year), it's inside the window but 'overdue=true' will render as a red Overdue badge on a birthday. Cosmetic: guard birthdays against the overdue flag.
server.py file is now 2729 lines — same feedback as iter17/18. Route explosion — split into routers.

Meetings.js:11 PROCESSING = ['queued','transcribing','structuring'] — if process_meeting throws before status is set to 'failed' (very unlikely — try/except handles it), refetchInterval would poll forever. Current implementation is safe because the outer try/except in process_meeting always sets status. Keep the failed status set-path.
Calendar.js:74 overdue check uses `day.date < new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)` — timezone-aware. Fine as long as backend uses UTC too (it does).

OperatingScore.js:83 employee filter `e.score != null || e.open > 0 || e.done > 0` — will hide members with zero data. That's intended, but on a fresh tenant the leaderboard could be empty. Consider showing at least the owner even with zero data.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter19 verified end-to-end: (1) POST /api/contacts/{id}/rescore [finance perm] — pulls invoices/payments/complaints/workflows for the contact, computes metrics {outstanding,total_billed,total_paid,last_payment,open_complaints,pending_deliveries,invoice_count,payment_count}, sends to ai_score_contact (Emergent LLM), caches on contact doc as ai_relationship={relationship_score,risk_score,reason,signals,scored_at}. Returns {ai_relationship}. Verified 401/403 for sales. (2) GET /api/contacts/{id}/profile — now surfaces ai_relationship in the returned dict. (3) GET /api/calendar?days=45 — returns {days:[{date,events[]}], counts:{type:n}, total}. Event types: payment_due (finance-only, unpaid sales_invoices), task (open+due_date), delivery (open sales_dispatch workflows w/ expected_date), complaint (uses created_at — always past), birthday (contact.birthday MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD, resolved to current year). Sorted asc by date; window -14d..+days. Verified sales returns counts.payment_due absent + no such events in days. (4) POST /api/contacts + PATCH accept optional birthday field; persisted verbatim. (5) POST /api/meetings/text {text} — creates {id, status:queued}, spawns background process_meeting that: (a) sets status=transcribing, (b) transcribes if audio, (c) status=structuring, (d) calls ai_meeting_notes → {title,summary,key_points[],decisions[],action_items[{title,assignee_name,due_in_days}]}, (e) inserts a task per action item (source=meeting, assignee resolved by match_member_by_name against user names for the tenant), (f) $set title/summary/etc + task_ids + status=done. Verified end-to-end: 1 transcript → done in ~10s → 3+ tasks created with source=meeting. POST /api/meetings (audio) reuses same pipeline via transcribe_audio (already tested elsewhere). (6) GET /api/operating-score — response shape {company:{overall,categories:{execution,finance,sales,responsiveness}}, stats:{done,open,overdue,total_decisions,approved,open_complaints,outstanding}, employees:[{id,name,role,score,done,open,overdue}], can_finance}. NOTE: the top-level layout is company/stats/employees/can_finance side-by-side, not everything nested inside `company` as the problem statement wording suggested — the frontend (OperatingScore.js:23) correctly destructures {company, stats, employees}. Non-finance users get outstanding=null (verified) BUT the `finance` category is still computed with defaults (collected=0.7 → finance=70), which is inconsistent with the money-hiding intent. Frontend testids all present: relationship-card, rescore-contact-btn, rel-relationship, rel-risk, rel-signals, cal-filter-all/task/payment_due/etc, cal-day-*, cal-event-*, meeting-record-button, meeting-paste-toggle, meeting-text-input, meeting-text-submit, meetings-list, meeting-card-*, meeting-dialog, operating-overall-score, operating-cat-*, operating-employees, operating-emp-*.
